findings.title: In-place image downsize can corrupt the uploaded file on failure
findings.body: The new auto-downsize code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, overwriting the original upload file in place, and ignores the boolean return value. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails partway through (unsupported or malformed image, missing delegate, killed process), the destination path may already be truncated or partially written. The loop then retries on the damaged file up to five times before `Upload.create_for` stores whatever remains, so a failed resize can turn a valid upload into a corrupt or empty file. The resize should write to a separate temporary path and atomically replace the original only on success, and the caller should stop/fail when conversion returns false.

findings.title: Animated GIF detection uses the tempfile path and strips animation
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` decides whether to use the animated conversion path by checking `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The controller passes `tempfile.path` as `from`; Rack upload tempfile paths normally have no `.gif` extension, even when the uploaded filename is `.gif`. As a result `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` has no effect for normal uploads: a large animated GIF falls back to `convert from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. The original upload then loses its animation (or the conversion fails). Animated handling should be based on the original filename/content type, not the tempfile path.

findings.title: Five fixed 80% passes may leave the image above max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The resize loop runs at most five times and then proceeds without checking whether the file is now within `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Five 80% linear resizes reduce area to roughly 10.7%, so a 10 MB image can remain above a 1 MB limit; for smaller configured limits the gap is larger. In that case `Upload.create_for` receives an oversized file and the upload either fails server-side validation or, if validation does not enforce this path, stores an image larger than the configured limit. The loop should verify the final size and fail explicitly if the target cannot be reached.

findings.title: Client upload limit is hardcoded instead of respecting site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10 MB limit for every upload type and no longer reads `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. For attachments this ignores the configured `max_attachment_size_kb`, allowing users to select files the server will reject; for images it also rejects images above 10 MB even if an administrator configured a larger limit. The 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports 10 MB instead of the configured limit, giving a misleading error message. The client should continue using the appropriate site setting where server-side auto-downsizing is not applicable.

findings.title: No tests cover the automatic image downsize path
findings.body: The PR adds a new server-side resize path and a new `OptimizedImage.downsize` overload but does not add tests. There is no coverage for oversized image reduction, non-image uploads, conversion failure behavior, or animated GIF handling. Those are exactly the paths where the in-place mutation and animation-detection issues above can regress unnoticed.
